elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained Para. B: "M&I shall indemnify Customer from, and defend Customer against, any liability or expenses..."; the preamble defines "Customer" as Tri City National Bank "(including its Affiliates)", so the defence duty runs to affiliates without added wording. New Para. C expressly extends "M&I's indemnity and defense obligations under Paragraph B" to the added limbs.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Para. B(i)-(ii) cover "any claim by a third party" and the defined term "Customer" already includes Affiliates per the preamble; no duplicate affiliate language added.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Para. B(i): "any claim by a third party that the Services or M&I's software infringe upon any United States patent, copyright or trademark of a third party." Coverage of Services/software IP infringement exists, though limited to U.S. patent/copyright/trademark (no trade secret or non-U.S. rights) - a sub-element shortfall noted rather than a failure of the element.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New Para. C(i): obligations "shall further extend to any liability or expenses arising out of or relating to (i) M&I's violation of applicable law", curing the prior limitation to protected-class statutes in B(iv).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New Para. C(ii): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer's data caused by M&I"; expressed as a descriptive phrase, so no undefined defined-term is introduced.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: New Para. C(iii): "M&I's gross negligence or wilful misconduct", both limbs present and unconditional.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Unchanged 14.3: "such indemnitee shall give notice of such claim to the indemnifying party, including a brief description of the amount and basis therefor, if known."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Unchanged 14.3: indemnifying party "shall be entitled to assume control of the defense of the claim with counsel chosen by the indemnifying party, reasonably satisfactory to the indemnitee."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Unchanged 14.3: "Indemnitee shall cooperate fully with, and assist, the indemnifying party in its defense against such claim in all reasonable respects."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Revised Para. A now reads only "(i) content, data, or materials provided by Customer to M&I and (ii) Customer's violation of applicable law"; the prior sweeping limbs (representation inaccuracy, protected-class laws, harassment, work injury, all property/financial loss, Section 6.6(B)) are removed, and 6.6 is "INTENTIONALLY OMITTED" so no dangling reference results.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Para. B(i) covers third-party claims that the Services or M&I's software infringe U.S. patent, copyright or trademark rights.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-modification exclusion is present, and none is required; the absence is more favourable to us, so the condition does not bite.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the clause contains no combination exclusion; nothing is required to be added.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: the clause contains no Customer-specification exclusion; nothing is required to be added.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Neither Para. B nor the new Para. C contains any procure/modify/replace remedy for an infringement finding; the rendered text has no such mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees fallback remedy appears anywhere in the rendered indemnity or procedures language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is stated; the only cap referenced elsewhere is Section 13.4's three-month liability cap, which is neither 3x annual fees nor an indemnity super-cap.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the retained Section 14.2(B) supplies the defend-and-indemnify duty and the IP limb, the preamble's "Customer (including its Affiliates)" carries the affiliate extension without duplicate wording, Section 14.3 supplies notice, control and cooperation, and the two edits add the missing conduct limbs (law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access/disclosure, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and narrow our own indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's violation of law.

Fallback level is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace remedy, no refund fallback, no 3x annual fees super-cap), so the finding correctly rests on the preferred level; the deviation classification stands because the incoming clause failed the fallback on remedies and super-cap.

Minimal: only Paragraph A's over-broad limbs were cut (each removal is required by the Customer-indemnity element) and a single concise Paragraph C was inserted for the three missing limbs. No survival tail, at-own-expense wording, extra damages categories, added procedures or affiliate duplication were introduced, and the favourable Section 14.3 procedures and Paragraph B limbs (ii)-(vii) are untouched.

Intent preserved: the enforcement-costs sentences in both paragraphs survive, Paragraph C cross-references Paragraph B correctly, dropping limb (vi) creates no orphan because Section 6.6 is "INTENTIONALLY OMITTED", and Section 13.4's liability cap and other commercial mechanics are left to the limitation-of-liability rule rather than contradicted here.

Residual (note in rationale, no operative repair required for completeness): the IP limb still reaches only "United States patent, copyright or trademark" claims, so trade-secret misappropriation and non-U.S. rights are uncovered; if pressed, the cleanest fix is to replace that phrase with "any intellectual property right" rather than adding a separate paragraph.

Optional drafting tightening: Paragraph C uses "Customer's data" while the agreement may use a defined data term elsewhere - align the wording if a defined term exists, to avoid an interpretive gap on scope.
